# Zelsis

> Zelsis checks every pull request before it merges, and fails the build when a critical bug gets in. It looks for security issues and for what users of the app would hit: payments that charge twice or the wrong amount, slow pages, migrations that lock the database during a deploy, screens that break on a phone or for keyboard users, App Store and Google Play review rejections, and pages that look unfinished (template titles, lorem ipsum, invented numbers or testimonials). Every scan gives two answers: Security, and Ready for users.

Zelsis works with JavaScript and TypeScript, Python, Go, Ruby, PHP, Java, C#, Rust, Swift, Kotlin, Flutter and React Native apps, SQL databases, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform and GitHub Actions. It runs as a GitHub App on pull requests or as a CI step. Code is scanned in memory and never stored; findings keep a short snippet, erased after 90 days. Pricing is one flat price per account, not per developer; there is a free plan.

## Product

- [Home](https://zelsis.com/): what Zelsis checks, an example failing pull request, pricing
- [Free site check](https://zelsis.com/site-check): enter a URL, no account; checks a live page for what a first visitor notices
- [Benchmark](https://zelsis.com/benchmark): every pinned open-source project scanned, what Zelsis finds and what it misses
- [Docs](https://zelsis.com/docs): setup for the GitHub App, CI and the API
- [Changelog](https://zelsis.com/changelog): what changed in what Zelsis finds
- [About](https://zelsis.com/about): who builds Zelsis and how results are measured
